why: The bulk-rename preview is computed TWICE: once in apps/files/core/src/bulk_rename.rs,
which performs the rename, and once in apps/files/src/lib/bulk-rename.ts, which draws the
dialog without a round-trip per keystroke. Nothing pinned them together, so a divergence
would show one name in the preview and write another - a wrong answer the person already
approved, on an operation that renames their files.
These vectors are the contract. The Rust test and the vitest test both run them, so the two
implementations cannot drift apart silently. The CORE is authoritative: if a case here
disagrees with it, the fixture is what was wrong, unless the core itself is.

cases.name: case insensitive find keeps the replacement verbatim
case transform applies to the whole name
numbering pads and substitutes both placeholders
a template without the number placeholder appends it
two names collapsing to one is a duplicate, not a silent overwrite
a separator in the result is refused rather than written
